title: Saturn Bomberman
subtitle: A roomful of rivals
summary: Saturn Bomberman is Hudson Soft's maze action game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 19 July 1996.
body: Saturn Bomberman is Hudson Soft's maze action game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 19 July 1996. Players place bombs in a grid of corridors, break soft blocks and try to catch opponents in the resulting explosions. Its most famous feature expands that familiar contest to ten players through multitap accessories. The larger gathering makes the arena a place of rapidly changing threats, where a bomb placed elsewhere can close an escape before the player has finished dealing with the danger immediately in front of them.

Bombs send fire along the maze's open lines, so choosing where to place one also means preserving a route away from it. Breaking blocks reveals more space and useful power-ups, changing the possibilities as a round continues. Dinosaur helpers hatch from eggs and can be ridden, providing special abilities and absorbing a hit for their rider. They grow through further collection, with the battle mode using additional eggs for that growth. The helper gives a vulnerable player another chance, but a crowded arena can consume that protection almost immediately.

Alongside competitive play, a story mode provides a sequence of stages, while Master mode asks the player to finish challenges quickly and records a rank. These modes let the same bomb placement support exploration, survival and measured performance. Jun Chikuma composed the soundtrack, maintaining the series' bright, energetic atmosphere. The ten-player battles remain the defining attraction because they magnify a remarkably clear rule: every player understands what a bomb will do, yet several people acting at once can turn a readable corridor into a trap in seconds.
